question.:question/worked-solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=5\log_{3} x$ and $v(x)=\ln x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & =(5\log_{3} x)^{′}\ln x+5\log_{3} x(\ln x)^{′} \\  & =(\frac{5}{x \ln{\left(3 \right)}})(\ln x)+(5\log_{3} x)(\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =\frac{5\log_{3} x}{x} + \frac{5\ln x}{x\ln 3}\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & =(\left(2 x^{3} - 5 x^{2}\right))^{′}\log_{6} x+\left(2 x^{3} - 5 x^{2}\right)(\log_{6} x)^{′} \\  & =\left(6 x^{2} - 10 x\right)\log_{6} x+\left(2 x^{3} - 5 x^{2}\right)\frac{1}{x\ln 6} \\  & =6{x}^{2}\log_{6} x-10x\log_{6} x+\frac{2{x}^{3}}{x\ln 6}-\frac{5{x}^{2}}{x\ln 6}\end{aligned}
